grh_01655a686a8a78716375.title: The Season of Glad Songs
paragraphs: Fifty-year-old Mildred has grown used to being treated as an outsider because she is unmarried and older than most of her coworkers. Her life changes when she begins seeing fifty-two-year-old Jim, whose companionship makes work and daily life feel lighter, and he soon asks her to marry him. Coworkers tease them and wedding businesses make Mildred painfully conscious of her age until she nearly calls off the ceremony, convinced that other people see their marriage as ridiculous. Jim reminds her that their love is real regardless of what strangers think. Mildred regains her confidence, and the story ends at their wedding with a reading from the Song of Solomon celebrating spring, renewal, and a love whose time has finally come.
